name: debug_find_accesses
description: Cheat-Engine style 'find out what writes/accesses this address': arms hardware watchpoints on free slots (length 1-32 split into aligned 1/2/4/8 slots, or struct mode: struct_span bytes from address watched by rotating the slots over rounds), resumes until timeout_seconds/max_hits, and collects unique accessing instructions (recovered by back-decoding to the post-access rip; confidence exact|ambiguous|plausible|unknown) with hit counts, disassembly, module+offset, offset/size/kind, sample registers and old/new values. Disarms its watchpoints on every exit path and leaves the target halted. Saves a ps4wb-access-v1 artifact (input for struct_infer).

length.description: Watched byte count (default 4); ignored in struct mode

access.description: write = what writes; read_write = what accesses (default write)

struct_span.description: Struct mode: watch [address, address+struct_span) in 32-byte rounds; time is split evenly across rounds

max_hits.description: Stop after this many in-range hits (default 256)

samples_per_instruction.description: Register/value samples kept per unique access (default 4)

name: struct_infer
description: Offline structure inference (read-only) from one or more ps4wb-access-v1 access logs, optional memory_snapshot artifacts of the object and optional read-only live sampling (pid + address). Infers fields (offset, size from operand size, type: pointer/vtable-like/code pointer via maps, float/double from SSE scalar instructions, bool/int widths, arrays from strided accesses) and emits a ps4wb-struct-v1 artifact with a C declaration.

snapshot_artifacts.description: memory_snapshot artifacts covering the object (aligned via their address metadata)

address.description: Object base (default: base of the first access log)

pid.description: Optional: read the object live (read-only) as an extra value sample

name: debug_crash_triage
description: Crash triage: analyze the current stop (wait=false) or resume and wait up to timeout_seconds for a fault stop (non-SIGTRAP FreeBSD wait status; SIGTRAP stops are skipped up to max_events). Collects signal, trapno/error code, live registers, faulting instruction with evaluated memory operands and their mapping/protection, stack trace, memory around rsp and operands, module+offset, and ranked classifications (null deref, wild read/write, write to read-only, execute non-exec/unmapped/outside modules, stack overflow, int3/ud2/abort, divide error). Never resumes after the fault; on timeout the target is halted. Saves a crash-report artifact.

wait.description: Resume and wait for a fault (default false: analyze the current stop)

thread_id.description: Thread to analyze (default: the stopping thread)

max_events.description: SIGTRAP stops to skip while waiting (default 64)

name: memory_pointer_scan
description: Read-only multi-level pointer scan: snapshots writable non-executable data maps (module data first, heaps if include_heap) within budget_bytes, indexes 8-byte aligned values that point into readable memory, and searches backward from target_address (max_depth <= 6, max_offset <= 0x4000) for paths rooted at static module locations ([module+off] -> +o1 -> +o2 ...). Saves a ps4wb-pointers-v1 artifact for memory_pointer_rescan.

include_heap.description: Also index anonymous/heap data maps (default true)

name: memory_pointer_rescan
description: Read-only rescan of a ps4wb-pointers-v1 artifact: re-resolves every saved path against current module bases and live memory (page-cached, bounded) and keeps those that still reach target_address (e.g. the new address after a game restart; default: the artifact's target). Saves the filtered paths as a new artifact.

name: debug_run_script
description: Host-side scripted breakpoints (Rhai, sandboxed): sets internal breakpoints, resumes, and on each hit calls the script's fn on_stop(ctx) which returns "continue"/"stop" (or true = stop / false = continue). ctx is read-only: ctx.reg(name), ctx.read_u8/u16/u32/i32/u64/f32/f64(addr), ctx.read_bytes(addr,n<=4096), ctx.read_cstring(addr,max<=4096), ctx.bp_name, ctx.bp_address, ctx.hits, ctx.total_hits, ctx.thread_id, ctx.rip, ctx.location, persistent ctx.state map (ctx.state.x = ..., ctx.get/ctx.set), log(msg)/print. No filesystem, network, process, import, eval or memory/register writes; operations, call depth, sizes, per-hit time and reads are bounded. Script errors stop the run. Breakpoints are cleared on every exit path and the target is left halted. Saves a script-log artifact.
